results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I submitted a Sultai (black-green-blue) self-mill brew, labelled as a brew, with the mana borrowed from the Golgari Roots shell.

**The combo:** Superior Spider-Man can enter as a copy of any creature card in a graveyard. Bringer of the Last Gift's sacrifice-and-reanimate effect only triggers "if you cast it," and you did cast Spider-Man. So a Spider-Man copying Bringer does the whole effect for 4 mana instead of 8. Every player sacrifices all their other creatures, then every player returns all creature cards already in their graveyard. Town Greeter and the other mill cards fill your graveyard first, so you get back far more than you lose.

**The plan:**
- **Turns 1–3:** Molt Tender and Llanowar Elves speed up your mana. Town Greeter, Dredger's Insight, Cache Grab and Overlord of the Balemurk (cast cheap for 2 mana) each mill four cards.
- **Bringer stuck in hand:** Kiora, Bitter Triumph or Awaken the Honored Dead let you discard it.
- **Turn 3–4:** Spider-Man copies Bringer. Your board resets, and the milled Overlords, Stormbroods, Greeters and Kioras come back. You're left with a 4/4 flier on top.

**Directions I considered:**
1. A Golgari Roots mill package with blue added for Spider-Man.
2. A Dimir (blue-black) deck that gets Bringer into the graveyard by discarding it.
3. A Sultai midrange deck borrowing Dimir Midrange's creatures.

I chose the first. Roots is the only proven shell that plays Town Greeter, and four-card mills find a Bringer and creatures to return at the same time.

**Things to know:**
- **No proven list:** no published list plays these three cards together, so this is untested.
- **The tool's 3.1% line figure:** the checker says you'll have drawn every card in my written line by turn 6 in only 3.1% of games. That figure needs all five named cards in hand. The combo itself only needs Spider-Man in hand plus a Bringer in the graveyard.
- **Odds of having Spider-Man:** without mulligans, you have a Spider-Man in hand by turn 4 about 53% of the time. You almost always (99.5%) have a card that mills or discards by then. Cache Grab, Dredger's Insight and Overlord can also put a milled Spider-Man into your hand, so you'll find it more often than 53% (the odds tool doesn't model that).
- **It helps the opponent too:** they also get back the creatures in their graveyard, so time it when their graveyard is thin.
- **Mana:** 21 lands plus six mana creatures, like Roots. The checker suggests 24 lands, but only because it counts Bringer's 8 cost. You're not meant to cast Bringer from your hand.
- **Rarely played cards:** I kept Kiora and Awaken the Honored Dead even though few real decks play them. Each one lets you discard a Bringer stuck in your hand, which the more popular alternatives can't do.
- **Sideboard:** it's aimed at the current field: Izzet Aggro, Vivi Cauldron and control decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
I built **Temur Landfall**. It's a brew on the Landfall deck's base (fetchlands, Tifa, Traveling Chocobo, Bristly Bill, Mossborn Hydra), with red added for Full Bore and blue for Spell Snare.

**The plan:** On turn 4, warp in Mightform Harmonizer for {2}{G}. Then cast Full Bore on it: it becomes a 7/6, and because it was warped it also gets trample and haste. Play Fabled Passage as your land drop: landfall doubles the power to 14. Crack Passage: the basic land it fetches triggers landfall again, for 28 trample damage. With four lands, Passage untaps the basic it fetched, so that land pays for Full Bore. If Traveling Chocobo is out, each land triggers landfall twice, so the numbers go much higher. Escape Tunnel and Evolving Wilds give the same two triggers per land, and Tifa and Mossborn Hydra are backup threats that also grow off land drops.

**Spell Snare's job:** it costs one blue mana and counters any spell with mana value 2. In this field that hits a lot: Get Lost, Abrade, Lightning Strike, Floodpits Drowner, Agatha's Soul Cauldron, Fear of Missing Out and Innkeeper's Talent. You hold it up to protect the turn you go off.

**Mana:** Fetchlands can grab a Mountain or Island, so the deck has 14 red sources, 14 blue and 22 green.

**Directions I considered:**
1. A Gruul warp deck built on Boros Aggro's Full Bore package, splashing blue.
2. Izzet Aggro's burn and creature package with green added for Harmonizer.
3. This one, chosen because fetchlands give two landfall triggers each. That turns Harmonizer's doubling into a real turn-4 kill, and neither aggro base can use it.

**Honest odds:**
- You'll have Harmonizer by turn 4 in about 53% of games, and a fetchland in about 86%. You'll have both in about 45%.
- The checker found you'll have every card in the full listed line by turn 4 in only about 2% of games (mulligans included). That number also requires Traveling Chocobo and Spell Snare, which the kill doesn't need.
- In most games you'll win more slowly, with Tifa, Hydra and Bill growing off land drops while you wait for Harmonizer.

The sideboard (Abrade, Burst Lightning, Seedship Impact, Negate, Surrak, Snakeskin Veil, Ghost Vacuum) targets the aggro decks, Agatha's Soul Cauldron and the control decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:
I built a Bant (green-white-blue) combo deck, labeled as a brew. Your three cards set up a loop that makes as many token creatures as you want.

**The combo:** Doc Aurlock, Grizzled Genius makes spells you cast from exile cost {2} less. "Airbend" exiles a card and lets you cast it again for {2}, so with Doc out, airbended cards cost nothing. The loop:
1. Appa, Steadfast Guardian enters and airbends Airbender Ascension.
2. You cast Ascension again for free. Because you cast it from exile, Appa makes a 1/1 Ally token.
3. When Ascension enters, it airbends Appa. You cast Appa again for free, and it airbends Ascension again.
4. Repeat as many times as you like.

Aang, Swift Savior can replace Ascension, and since both Aang and Appa have flash, you can run that version at the end of your opponent's turn. Every Ally that enters makes Haru, Hidden Talent turn a land into a creature with haste and a +1/+1 counter. It also gives Earth King's Lieutenant a +1/+1 counter, and the Lieutenant has trample. Either way you get a creature big enough to win in one attack.

**Bramble Familiar** makes mana, so you can cast Appa on turn 3. Late in the game, its Fetch Quest side mills seven cards and puts a creature or enchantment from them onto the battlefield, which can find a missing combo piece.

**Directions I considered:**
- The 5-color Temur Battlecrier list, the only real list that runs all three cards. Its mana base is too stretched.
- Your cards added to the Selesnya Offense creature package. It has no way to actually win with them.
- This deck: Doc Aurlock plus the loop, with the mana dorks (Llanowar Elves) and a mana base adapted from Selesnya Offense.

I chose the last one because it's the only option where your three cards win the game together instead of just giving small value.

**Things to know:**
- **Combo odds:** Without mulligans, you'll have drawn Doc, Appa and a loop partner by turn 5 in about 24% of games.
- **Without the combo:** In other games the deck plays as a fair midrange deck. You have flash flyers, 4 Get Lost, and Appa or Ascension reusing the "enters" effects of your creatures for {2} each.
- **Mana:** The deck has 17 green sources, while real Selesnya Offense lists run about 21.7. That's on purpose: they're nearly mono-green, and this deck needs white (Appa costs WW) and blue too.
- **Unproven lands:** Hallowed Fountain and Temple Garden are legal but haven't shown up in recent results.

The sideboard is aimed at the current meta: Annul and Rest in Peace against Vivi Cauldron and Reanimator, Tishana's Tidebinder against Dimir, and Dazzling Angel and Seam Rip against the aggro decks.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Abandon Attachments, Firebending Lesson and Combustion Technique.
results.text:
I built **Izzet Lessons Tempo** as a brew, and it was accepted as legal. I took the red cards and lands from Izzet Aggro, which is 12% of the field.

**The plan:** Cheap threats come down early: Hired Claw on turn 1, then First-Time Flyer, Sokka and Dragonfly Swarm. Your three Lessons do double duty. Firebending Lesson (2 damage for R, or 5 kicked) and Combustion Technique clear blockers. Abandon Attachments turns a spare land into two new cards. Every Lesson that hits your graveyard also makes something bigger:
- First-Time Flyer gets +1/+1 once you have a Lesson in the graveyard.
- Sokka gets a +1/+1 counter each time you cast a Lesson.
- Dragonfly Swarm's power equals your noncreature, nonland cards in the graveyard.
- Combustion Technique deals 2 damage plus 1 for each Lesson in your graveyard, and it exiles what it kills.

Nova Hellkite (hasty 4-power flier) and Burst Lightning to the face finish the game, usually around turn 6. The deck runs 13 Lessons (4 of each requested card plus 1 Iroh's Demonstration). On the play you have about a 91% chance to see a Lesson by turn 3. The odds of seeing a Lesson and one of the 11 creatures that grow from them by then are about 78%.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Mono-Red Firebending.** This is the only real list that runs all three cards. It's a single Mono-Red deck from a Standard Challenge, and Mono-Red is 0.2% of the field. There the Lessons are just cheap burn with no reward for stacking them up.
2. **Izzet Lessons Tempo, using Izzet Aggro's red package (chosen).**
3. **Blue-heavy Lessons control** with Accumulate Wisdom, Sokka's Haiku and Serpent of the Pass. It's slow and has fewer good creatures.

I chose option 2 because blue adds three creatures that grow with your Lessons. That makes the Lessons an engine, and the borrowed burn and lands are proven against this field.

**Things to know:**
- Screaming Nemesis appears in the menu's Izzet and Boros lists, but it is banned in Standard now, so I left it out.
- The deck has only 17 red sources, compared with about 21.5 in real Izzet Aggro lists. That's on purpose: 11 of the cheap creatures need blue, so the deck plays 13 blue sources.

The 15-card sideboard is aimed at the main decks in the field:
- **Sunspine Lynx and Magebane Lizard:** against Dimir and Vivi.
- **Iroh's Demonstration:** against go-wide decks like Ouroboroid and Boros.
- **Soul-Guide Lantern:** against Reanimator and Vivi Cauldron.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
I built an Izzet Elementals ramp-tempo deck. It's a brew, using Izzet Aggro's mana base and burn.

**The plan:** Ashling (and Flamebraider) ramp you into a big Elemental like Deceit or Ice Flan by turn 4. Sunderflock costs less by the mana value of your biggest Elemental, so with Deceit (mana value 6) out it costs just {1}{U}{U} on turn 5. When it enters it returns every non-Elemental creature to its owner's hand. Every creature in this deck is an Elemental, so only the opponent's board goes back. Bounce Off, Burst Lightning and Lightning Strike keep you alive until then. After the big bounce, Bounce Off sends back whatever they replay while the 5/5 fliers attack.

**What each requested card does here:**
- **Ashling, Rekindled:** When it enters, you can discard a card to draw one (good for an extra Sunderflock). On turn 3 you pay {U} to flip it into Ashling, Rimebound. Rimebound adds two mana every turn for spells with mana value 4 or more. Sunderflock still counts as mana value 9 after its discount, so that mana can pay for it.
- **Sunderflock:** The finisher and the one-sided board reset. Ten big Elementals set up the discount (4 Deceit, 2 Ice Flan, 2 Wistfulness, 2 Twinflame Travelers).
- **Bounce Off:** One-mana tempo before and after the big turn.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Izzet Elementals (chosen):** Ashling is red, and Deceit, Wistfulness and Sunderflock can all be paid with blue only. Two colours with Steam Vents, Spirebluff Canal and Riverpyre Verge gave the most reliable mana of the three options.
2. **Grixis Superior Spider-Man:** This borrows the Reanimator package. Spider-Man copies a Deceit in the graveyard and gets you to a turn-4 Sunderflock. It's faster when it works, but it needs three colours plus the graveyard setup.
3. **Temur with Llanowar Elves and Wistfulness:** This borrows the Ouroboroid shell. Most of the green cards would be bounced by your own Sunderflock.

**Things to know:**
- The checker wanted me to build on the "Rogue" lists. That label is a catch-all: its latest list is an unrelated Allies deck. The few Rogue lists with Sunderflock are a four-colour reanimator deck with no Ashling or Bounce Off, so I didn't use that shell.
- **Odds:** You see at least one Ashling or Flamebraider by turn 3 75% of the time. You have Sunderflock plus a big Elemental by turn 5 about 50% of the time. The exact winning line needs all four specific cards (Ashling, Deceit, Sunderflock, Bounce Off) by turn 6, which happens only about 9% of the time. In practice you swap in other pieces: Ice Flan for Deceit, Flamebraider for Ashling.
- **Lands:** The deck runs 23, slightly under the 24.4 the checker suggests. The 8 two-drops that make mana and Ice Flan's islandcycling make up for it.

The 15-card sideboard covers the main decks in the field: graveyard hate, counterspells, sweepers, artifact removal and Sunspine Lynx.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Insatiable Avarice, Doomsday Excruciator and Archenemy's Charm.

I built a **mono-black "Doomsday" control deck**, borrowing the mana base and removal suite from the Mono-Black lists in recent results (24 lands, 21–24 black sources). No published list plays all three of your cards together, so this is a brew.

**The plan:** Kill their creatures and strip their hand with removal and discard (Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff, Duress, Deep-Cavern Bat) until turn 5–6.
- **Find the Demon:** On turn 5, cast Insatiable Avarice with both modes (5 mana) aimed at yourself. It puts Doomsday Excruciator on top of your library, then you draw three, so the Demon goes straight into your hand.
- **Cast it:** Doomsday Excruciator cuts both libraries down to six cards. The opponent draws first after that, so they run out before you do even if the Demon is removed.
- **Finish:** A held Avarice aimed at the opponent makes them draw three, leaving them two cards from losing. Bloodletter of Aclazotz is the backup kill. It doubles life loss on your turn, so each 6/6 Excruciator hit deals 12 and Avarice drains 6. Archenemy's Charm exiles blockers, gives the Demon +2/+2 and lifelink, or brings it back from the graveyard.

1. **Mono-Black Doomsday control (chosen):** your two cards that need lots of black (BBBBBB, BBB) work best with 24 black sources.
2. **Mono-Black aggro with Bloodletter:** Avarice works as a 6-point burn spell here, but a 6-drop doesn't fit an aggro deck.
3. **Dimir control:** borrows Stock Up and Three Steps Ahead from the Dimir lists, but two-colour mana can't reliably cast Excruciator on turn 6.

I chose the first because it turns Excruciator's library exile from a drawback into the win condition.

- **Hold an Avarice before casting the Demon.** Any Avarice left in your library gets exiled with the rest, so keep one in hand.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Resonating Lute, Inevitable Defeat and Jeskai Revelation.
results.text:
I built a 4-colour Jeskai control deck that splashes black, with Resonating Lute as both the ramp and the colour fixer. Lute makes every land tap for two mana of any one colour, but only for instants and sorceries. That's what makes the other two cards work: you can pay Inevitable Defeat's R, W and B (red, white, black) from any lands, and four lands pay for the 7-mana Jeskai Revelation. With five or six lands you can often cast both in one turn and still keep No More Lies up.

The early game uses the proven Jeskai Control package: Lightning Helix, No More Lies, Get Lost and Day of Judgment keep you alive. Consult the Star Charts and Stock Up dig for Lute. The win is slow: Inevitable Defeat drains 3 each time and can't be countered, Revelation deals 4 and makes Monk tokens, Helix finishes, and Lute's draw ability (it only works with seven or more cards in hand) means you won't run out of cards.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **Chosen: Jeskai Control plus a black splash.** It's the menu deck that already plays Revelation, and the only one where real lists run Lute (4 of the 5 Lute lists are Jeskai Control).
2. **Mardu control without blue.** Rejected because Revelation and Lute both need blue.
3. **Lute as ramp for big sorceries like Ultima or Omniscience.** Rejected because it pushes your three cards out of the centre.

I picked 1 because real players already run Defeat with Revelation, Helix and No More Lies (the Defeat lists are listed as "Rogue"), so the shell is proven. All I added was Lute and a few black lands.

**Notes on the build:**
- **Black sources:** there are 8 lands that make black. Four are Great Hall of the Biblioplex, which makes any colour for instants and sorceries; Defeat is an instant. The others are 2 Godless Shrine, 1 Watery Grave and 1 Blood Crypt, and Lute adds more black once it's out.
- **Lute copies:** I went to 4 Lute. With 3 copies you had only about a 50% chance of drawing one by turn 6; the fourth replaces a Seam Rip.
- **Three Steps Ahead** can make a token copy of Lute.
- **Revelation copies:** I kept 3, like the Jeskai Control lists. Two 7-drops in an early hand is a dead card.
- **The mana check passed** with no warnings. The deck runs 26 lands with 19 white, 19 blue, 13 red and 8 black sources, close to real Jeskai Control lists.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Arclight Phoenix, Buried Alive and Flow State.
results.text:
I built a **Grixis Ritual Phoenix** brew (blue-black-red). It's a combo deck: get three Arclight Phoenixes into the graveyard early, then cast three cheap instants or sorceries in one turn so all three come back.

**The plan:** On turn 2 (turn 1 with Lotus Petal), cast Dark Ritual, then Buried Alive to put three Phoenixes into the graveyard. Then cast one more cheap spell, like Ponder, Lava Dart or Manamorphose. That's three instants and sorceries, so at the start of combat all three Phoenixes return with flying and haste and hit for 9. They hit for 9 again next turn, and Lava Dart (cast once, then again by sacrificing a Mountain-type land) or Lightning Bolt finishes the game around turn 3. If the Phoenixes get removed, any later turn with three spells brings them back.

**What each requested card does here:**
- **Arclight Phoenix** is the only creature and the whole win condition.
- **Buried Alive** puts three Phoenixes into the graveyard at once. Dark Ritual and Lotus Petal pay for it early, and it counts as one of the three spells.
- **Flow State** is the card-finding engine. Almost everything in the deck is an instant or sorcery, so it nearly always lets you keep two of the top three cards. That digs for Buried Alive or Faithless Looting, and it counts toward the three spells too.

**Directions I considered:**
1. A slower Izzet Tempo build (blue-red) with Phoenix as one threat among several, splashing black.
2. A Rakdos (black-red) Faithless Looting and burn deck. Flow State needs blue, so this didn't fit.
3. A fast black ritual combo shell that borrows the Force of Will, Brainstorm, Ponder and Bolt package from Izzet Tempo, which is 8% of the field.

**I chose the third.** Buried Alive is only worth its 3 mana if it's cast early. Rituals make a turn-2 kill with three Phoenixes possible, and Force of Will protects it.

**Things to know:**
- **Odds:** you see Buried Alive or Faithless Looting (the backup for discarding Phoenixes) by turn 3 about 75% of the time without card draw. Brainstorm, Ponder and Flow State raise that. The checker says you'll have drawn every card in the exact line by turn 3 only about 1% of the time, but it doesn't count card draw or substitutes. Any cheap spell can be the third spell, so the real chance of the kill is much higher than that.
- **Land count:** the deck runs 16 lands, below the ~19 that Izzet Tempo plays. That's on purpose: the 4 Lotus Petals and 4 Dark Rituals also make mana.
- **Lava Dart:** the lands include 6 duals that count as Mountains (Volcanic Island and Badlands), plus 5 fetch lands that can find them, so you can usually cast Lava Dart a second time from the graveyard.
- **Graveyard hate:** the deck is weak to cards that empty or exile graveyards. Surgical Extraction is common in the current field.
- **Sideboard:** it's aimed at the current top decks. Pyroblast, Hydroblast and Thoughtseize are for the tempo decks and Sneak and Show. Blood Moon is for Tron and Lands. Fatal Push and Fiery Confluence are for Ocelot Aggro. Tormod's Crypt is for Reanimator and Oops All Spells.

results.prompt: Brew me a Vintage deck built around Goblin Welder, Legion Extruder and Sewer-veillance Cam.
results.text:
I built a blue-red (Izzet) Welder combo deck around a two-card loop. The deck passed the legality check and was accepted. It's a brew: nobody has played this deck in Vintage yet. The only real lists running all three cards are a Legacy deck called "Sewer Combo."

**How the loop works**
- Goblin Welder swaps an artifact you control with an artifact card in your graveyard.
- Sewer-veillance Cam untaps a creature both when it enters and when it leaves the battlefield.
- So with Cam on the battlefield and Legion Extruder in the graveyard, Welder can swap them back and forth. Every swap untaps Welder for free, and every time Extruder enters it deals 2 damage. You can repeat this as many times as you want, so it kills the opponent.

The usual setup is Welder on turn 1. On turn 2, Goblin Engineer puts Extruder into your graveyard when it enters, then you cast Cam for one blue mana and start looping. Other ways to get the pieces in place:
- Melded Moxite and Thirst for Knowledge let you discard Cam or Extruder.
- Tinker can sacrifice Cam to put Extruder onto the battlefield.
- Extruder's own ability sacrifices Cam as its cost.
- Skateboard gives Welder haste.

**The three directions I considered**
1. **Port the Legacy deck as-is.** Mono-red artifacts with Painter's Servant and Grindstone as a second combo.
2. **Workshop Welder.** Use Mishra's Workshop for fast mana. But Workshop's mana can only cast artifacts, and Welder and Engineer are creatures, so it doesn't help cast them.
3. **Izzet Welder (chosen).** Keep the Legacy engine and add the blue package from the top decks (Lurrus PO and Lurrus Control): the Power cards, 4 Force of Will, Mental Misstep and Force of Negation, plus 3 Pyroblast against the blue decks. I picked this because Cam, Fabricate, Tinker and the blue draw spells are blue cards you can exile to pay for Force of Will. That lets a fragile one-mana Welder combo protect itself in a field full of Force of Will decks.

**Honest odds**
- On the draw, you have Welder, a Cam source (Cam or Fabricate) and an Extruder source (Extruder, Engineer or Tinker) all in hand by turn 3 about 23% of the time. That figure ignores Ancestral Recall, Brainstorm, Moxite, Thirst and Time Walk, which raise it.
- Drawing the exact turn-2 sequence with no tutors happens about 1% of the time. Expect turn 2 to be the best case; the deck usually takes longer.
- When the loop isn't ready, Extruder still works as removal (2 damage when it enters) and turns spare artifacts into 3/3 Golems.

**Sideboard**
It's aimed at the decks the meta data shows: Tormod's Crypt, Soul-Guide Lantern and Grafdigger's Cage against Dredge and Oath, Red Elemental Blast and Mindbreak Trap against the blue decks, and Abrade, Fiery Confluence and Pithing Needle against Shops.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Ardent Recruit, Search Party Captain and Springleaf Drum.
results.text:
I built a Boros artifact go-wide deck. There are 22 creatures that cost 1–2 mana, and 24 artifacts to turn on Ardent Recruit's metalcraft (+2/+2 with three or more artifacts): 10 artifact lands, 4 Springleaf Drum, 4 Experimental Synthesizer and 6 Inspectors that make Clue tokens. You flood the board early and swing wide, which makes Search Party Captain cost 1–2 mana and draw you a card. Lightning Bolt and a 4-damage Galvanic Blast clear blockers or finish the opponent.

**What each requested card does here**
- **Ardent Recruit:** A 1-drop that becomes a 3/3 by turn 2. For example: Ancient Den, then Drum, then Thraben Inspector's Clue makes three artifacts.
- **Springleaf Drum:** Taps any creature for mana, even one you just cast, so you can play two cheap spells a turn. It also counts toward metalcraft and fixes your colors. Glint Hawk and Kor Skyfisher can return it to your hand to recast for 1, keeping your artifact count up.
- **Search Party Captain:** Your card advantage. After attacking with three creatures it costs only 1 mana; cast it after combat and pay with Drum.

**Directions I considered**
1. Mono-white aggro from the menu, using Inspectors and Battle Screech.
2. Orzhov Glintblade, with Cast Down and Refurbished Familiar.
3. The Boros artifact shell taken from the Synthesizer deck (57 lists in recent results).

I chose the Boros shell. Red adds Great Furnace and Rustvale Bridge as extra artifact lands, plus burn that gets stronger with metalcraft. Mono-white only has Ancient Den as an artifact land. No published list plays these three cards together, so this is a real brew. The mana, removal and sideboard come from Synthesizer lists, and the requested cards replace its Lembas and Melded Moxite.

**Things to know**
- I run 18 lands, while Synthesizer lists average about 20.5. That's because the average mana value here is 1.48, the Captain usually costs 1–2, and the four Drums work as extra mana.
- The sample turn-5 kill (Recruit → Drum + Inspector → Glint Hawk → Captain → Blast) shows how the deck plays. Drawing those exact cards is rare (about 0.6% of games). The deck relies on having many interchangeable cheap creatures and artifacts.
- You'll draw a Recruit by turn 3 in about 49% of games. You'll almost always (99%) have other artifacts to go with it.
- Artifact lands are weak to artifact removal, which the format has plenty of (Krark-Clan Shaman and Cleansing Wildfire both show up in current lists).
- The sideboard is aimed at Terror and Faeries (Red Elemental Blast), Affinity and other artifact decks (Dust to Dust), Madness (Electrickery, Prismatic Strands), and graveyard decks (Relic of Progenitus).

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
I built a **Boros Graveyard Spirits** brew (Pauper). Nobody has published a list that plays these three cards together, so it's untested.

**The plan:** Aurora Eidolon and Sandstorm Eidolon both come back to your hand from the graveyard whenever you cast a multicolored spell. Spirit Mascot is itself a red/white multicolored spell, and it gets a +1/+1 counter every time cards leave your graveyard. So the deck:
- discards the Eidolons on purpose with Faithless Looting, Thrilling Discovery and Pursue the Past;
- gets them back by casting multicolored cards (Mascot, Discovery, Pursue the Past, Skyknight Legionnaire);
- grows Mascot with flashback spells (Looting, Battle Screech, Rally the Peasants, Pursue the Past), Lunarch Veteran's disturb, Sneaky Snacker coming back, and the Eidolons themselves returning.

Each Eidolon is reusable once in play. Sacrifice Sandstorm for {R} so a blocker can't block, or Aurora for {W} to prevent 3 damage (for example, to save Mascot from Lightning Bolt). Either one comes back with your next multicolored spell. The planned kill is a wide board of birds and spirits pumped by Rally the Peasants and its flashback on turn 5. The checker says you'll almost never draw every card in that exact sequence by turn 5. Treat it as the shape of a typical win, not a fixed script.

**Directions I considered:**
1. **What I chose:** borrow the Boros Aggro package from recent results (4 Looting, Thrilling Discovery, Battle Screech, Rally, Sneaky Snacker, Boros Garrison mana).
2. A Lorehold Pledgemage spells deck.
3. A three-color version adding red/green hybrid cards.

I picked the first because that proven shell already does both things these cards need: it puts cards in the graveyard and then pulls them back out. Sneaky Snacker is blue/black, but this deck never casts it. You discard it, and it returns to play when you draw your third card in a turn, which Thrilling Discovery does by itself. That also gives Mascot a counter.

**Things to know:**
- The deck has 13 white sources. Real Boros Aggro lists run about 16. I moved some of that toward red because Mascot and the other multicolored cards need red early.
- The sideboard (Red Elemental Blast, Pyroblast, Dust to Dust, Electrickery, Prismatic Strands, Thraben Charm) is aimed at Madness, Terror and Affinity, the biggest decks in the field.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Living Death.
results.text:
**BG Living Death (brew, Premodern)**

**The plan:** Fill your graveyard with big creatures, then cast Living Death. It forces every player to sacrifice all their creatures, then returns every creature card from your graveyard. That wipes the opponent's board and gives you a board of huge creatures in one spell.
- **Filling the graveyard:**
  - Buried Alive puts any three creatures into your graveyard.
  - Each time you use Survival of the Fittest, you discard a creature and search for another.
  - Wild Mongrel can discard creatures for free.
  - Krosan Tusker and Twisted Abomination can be discarded with cycling to fetch you a land.
- **Speed:** Dark Ritual and Birds of Paradise let you cast Living Death (5 mana) as early as turn 3–4.
- **Protection:** Duress and Cabal Therapy take counterspells out of the opponent's hand. Stiflenought, the most common deck right now (15% of the field), counters spells.
- **The main win:** Bring back Akroma with haste for 6 flying damage the turn she returns. Symbiotic Wurm and Verdant Force leave tokens behind even if they're removed. A second Living Death sacrifices the Wurm, which leaves you its 7 insect tokens.

**Three directions I considered:**
1. **Reanimator with Living Death added in.** This used the format's Reanimator cards: Putrid Imp, Exhume, Reanimate. Living Death would just have been a slower version of those spells.
2. **Hermit Druid self-mill.** Hermit Druid would put most of the deck into the graveyard, then Living Death returns it. It falls apart whenever Druid is removed, and Living Death would be a backup plan instead of the main one.
3. **The BG Survival shell with Living Death at the center (chosen).** Recent results show Living Death most often in this deck. I added Buried Alive and Dark Ritual from Reanimator. I picked it because Survival of the Fittest keeps filling the graveyard every turn, so each Living Death returns more creatures and also clears the opponent's board.

**Things to know:**
- **Mana:**
  - The deck runs 20 lands. The deck checker wanted about 23, but you never cast the 7-mana creatures. Birds, Rituals and the land-fetching cycling creatures make up the gap.
  - The checker warned that Akroma (white) and Squee (red) have no matching colored mana. That's on purpose: Akroma only enters through Living Death, and Squee is only something to discard to Survival, since he returns to your hand from the graveyard every upkeep.
- **Your odds:** With no mulligans, you have about a 53% chance to draw a Living Death by turn 4. Survival can only find creatures, so it can't search for Living Death; that is the deck's main weakness. Mongrel, the cycling creatures and Bone Shredder let you play a normal game while you wait. The checker reported only 0.1% for drawing every card in the win line by turn 5. That number ignores Survival and Buried Alive, which are how you get Akroma and the Wurm into the graveyard, so it understates the real chance.
- **Watch out for:**
  - Living Death also returns the opponent's dead creatures. That matters most against Sligh and Goblins.
  - Graveyard removal shuts the deck down. The sideboard has Tormod's Crypt and Withered Wretch for opposing graveyard decks. It also has Engineered Plague for Goblins and Elves, Naturalize for Enchantress and Replenish, and Ravenous Baloth and Spike Feeder against Sligh.
